description: Eclipse Ditto is an open-source framework for building digital twins of devices connected to the internet. It acts as IoT middleware that represents each physical device as a digital twin, manages its reported, desired and current state, enforces access control, and offers synchronous and asynchronous APIs. It connects to other systems over HTTP with webhooks, MQTT 3.1.1 and 5, AMQP 0.9.1 and 1.0 and Apache Kafka 2.x, with payload mapping so that devices and backends using arbitrary formats can be integrated. It is developed as a project of the Eclipse Foundation. It is generic, not tied to a sector or region, and is used in industrial IoT, energy and building applications. The software is free and open source under the Eclipse Public License 2.0 and is self-hosted. Caveats: it manages device state and messaging, not physics or process models, so simulation logic must be added separately, and the home page read does not state the current version or deployment tooling. For simulation it is a building block for digital twins that keep models in sync with live sensor data and push control commands back to devices. It is related to the AWS IoT TwinMaker record in this catalogue, a managed cloud alternative.
